name: Valentin Borisovich Aleskovskii
summary: Soviet and Russian chemist, founder of the Molecular Layering method and the 'Chemistry of highly organized substances' school.

name: Stanislav Ivanovich Kol'tsov
summary: Chemist and graduate student of Aleskovskii, co-founder of the Molecular Layering method.

name: Anatolii A. Malygin
summary: Chemist, student of Aleskovskii, author of the essay.

name: Victor E. Drozd
summary: Physicist and student of Aleskovskii, developed vacuum ML equipment.

name: Tuomo Suntola
summary: Finnish physicist, inventor of Atomic Layer Epitaxy (ALE).

name: Leningrad Technological Institute by Lensovet
aliases: St. Petersburg State Technological Institute (Technical University)
summary: Educational and research institute where Aleskovskii and Kol'tsov developed ML.

name: Leningrad State University
summary: University where Aleskovskii served as rector and founded the Solid State Chemistry Department.

name: Academy of Sciences of the USSR
summary: Highest scientific body in the Soviet Union.

name: Framework Hypothesis
summary: Theory proposed by Aleskovskii in 1952 describing solids as supramolecules with a core and functional groups.

name: Molecular Layering Method
summary: Gas-phase layer-by-layer deposition technique developed in the Soviet Union.

name: Atomic Layer Epitaxy
summary: Thin-film deposition method invented by Suntola in Finland.

name: Chemistry of highly organized substances
summary: Scientific school founded and supervised by Aleskovskii.

name: Chemical assembly of materials
summary: Inter-university program founded in 1978 under Aleskovskii's supervision.

name: Mary
summary: City in Turkmenistan where Aleskovskii was born.

name: Leningrad
summary: City where Aleskovskii worked and studied.
